mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY > 2% does not correlate with subsequent Fed tightening actions.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points within a month signals a tightening labor market, which historically leads to increased wage pressures and inflation expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the drop in UNRATE does not correlate with subsequent inflationary pressures.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in Real Final Sales of Domestic Product (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or RSAFS MoM > 1% does not correlate with subsequent earnings growth.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) by more than 2% year-over-year signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to concerns about economic slowdown.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO YoY < -2% does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdown.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is rising, it signals a period of accommodative monetary policy with inflationary pressure, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the combination of low FEDFUNDS and rising CPIAUCSL does not correlate with subsequent positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 300,000 in a month signals strong labor market conditions, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS increase > 300k does not correlate with subsequent consumer confidence and spending growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increase does not correlate with subsequent economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: When Industrial Production (INDPRO) is declining and Real GDP (GDPC1) is stagnant, it signals a supply-side slowdown, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to concerns about economic contraction.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of declining INDPRO and stagnant GDPC1 does not correlate with subsequent economic contraction.
